summary: Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1923–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gaden Chokhor Monastery and Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundrup Tabkhe and others, later serving as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967.

Geshe Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery, founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, and served as its director until 1997.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin held posts at Central Schools for Tibetans, served as Principal and Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and later became Chancellor of Sanchi University.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Mey Monastery, earning a Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2010, his posts include Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and an affiliation with the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Drepung Monastery (attested 1966 and 1976), Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1995), and Leiden University.

Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi, an affiliation attested between 1987 and 1992, and was also attested there in 2004.

Geshe Rabten (1920–1986) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, earning a Geshe Lharampa degree, and taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from around 1969 to 1974.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, becoming resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 1978.

Geshe Tashi Tsering (born 1958) studied at Sera Monastery and Gyuto Monastery, later studying under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he taught at Kopan Monastery and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.
Geshe Tsondru Kongpel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned Geshe degrees while studying at both Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal (1901–1983) studied at Drepung Monastery and under Agvan Dorzhiev. A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he directed the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center from circa 1958 to 1983 and taught at Columbia University from circa 1960 to 1972.

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (born 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. His career includes posts as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991, 2004, and 2014–2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche, later teaching philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1968–1970).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin pursued traditional monastic studies under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Otani University under Manshi Kiyozawa, later serving at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) studied at Sapienza University of Rome, specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza University of Rome (1993–2008).

Ghulam Yazdani (1885–1962) was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Aligarh Muslim University under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi. He directed the Archaeological Department of Hyderabad State from circa 1914 to 1943.

Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1992.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.
